intended_object: A Hölder triple of finite nonnegative exponents: p, q, r with p, q > 0 and 1/p + 1/q = 1/r, the exponent condition in Hölder's inequality ‖fg‖_r ≤ ‖f‖_p‖g‖_q. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The structure asks for p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = r⁻¹ together with 0 < p and 0 < q. These two conditions force r⁻¹ > 0, so r > 0. That means the junk value 0⁻¹ = 0 in ℝ≥0 can never come into play, and the definition matches the textbook condition exactly. Mathlib's design gives this notion separate parallel versions on ℝ (`Real.HolderTriple`), ℝ≥0 (this one) and ℝ≥0∞ (`ENNReal.HolderTriple`, which also allows infinite exponents), each tied to the others by coercion lemmas such as `holderTriple_coe_iff`. This follows the same pattern as `IsConjExponent`/`HolderConjugate`. The ℝ≥0 version is one of these deliberate type-specific variants for finite nonnegative exponents, so it is not an overly narrow restatement of something more general.
